title: Reformat Phone Number
statement:
The string `number` is a phone number written with digits, spaces and dashes. Reformat it as follows and return the result:

1. Keep only the digits, in their original order.
2. Working from the left, cut off blocks of three digits as long as more than four digits are left.
3. The two, three or four digits that remain form the end: two or three digits make one final block, while four digits make two blocks of two.
4. Join all the blocks with single dashes.

No block ever ends up with just one digit.
constraints: number contains at least two digits
notes:
## Intuition

Only the digits matter, and the block sizes depend only on how many digits there are. Taking blocks of three greedily works until four or fewer digits are left; stopping at four (instead of three) is what prevents a lonely one-digit block, because four digits are split as two plus two.

## Approach

1. Remove every non-digit character to get `digits`.
2. While more than four digits remain after `start`, push the next three as a block and advance `start` by 3.
3. Let `remaining` be the count left. If it is 4, push two blocks of two; otherwise push the rest (2 or 3 digits) as one block.
4. Join `blocks` with `'-'`.

## Example 1, step by step

`"1-23-45 6"` becomes `digits = "123456"`. Six digits is more than four, so `"123"` is pushed and `start = 3`. Now `remaining = 3`, which is not more than four, so `"456"` is pushed as one block. Joining gives `"123-456"`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass to filter, one to cut blocks, one to join.
- Space: O(n) for `digits` and the blocks.

## Pitfalls

- Stopping the loop at "three or fewer left" breaks the four-digit case: `"1234"` must become `"12-34"`, not `"123-4"`.
- Spaces and dashes can appear anywhere, including at the start, at the end and in runs; remove all of them first.
- Two digits form a single block of two; do not split them further.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `digits` | the input with only its digits kept |
| `blocks` | the groups built so far |
| `start` | index of the first digit not yet placed in a block |
| `remaining` | how many digits are left for the final part |

narration.2: Strip spaces and dashes so only the digits are left.
narration.5: Keep cutting blocks of three while more than four digits are still unplaced.
narration.6: The next three digits form one block.
narration.7: Move past the digits just used.
narration.9: Count the 2, 3 or 4 digits left for the ending.
narration.10: Four digits cannot be one block and must not leave a single digit...
narration.11: ...so they become a first block of two...
narration.14: Two or three digits form one final block.
narration.16: Join every block with a dash.
